notes: Low vowel dissimilation, left to right, in all Southern Vanuatu languages; root-initial *q blocks it (the article *na-qa > na), *r does not (§4.1.4-4.1.5). Blocked by velars, postvelars and labiovelars before or after the *a, with exceptions (§5.2). The same row is in the data from Lynch (2001: 99).
Unstressed *a dissimilated 'sometimes as e, sometimes as zero'; stressed *a as e (§4.1.3). The e row is in the data from Lynch (2000b).

Historical dissimilation in both northern and southern Paamese, stressed or unstressed (stress irrelevant), apparently right to left; the fused article *a does not dissimilate except before *qa (§4.2.1). Blocked by velars, postvelars and labiovelars before or after the *a, with exceptions (§5.2).
As in Paamese, apparently right to left; the data are limited (§4.2.2).
Neve'ei: secondary-stressed and unstressed *a dissimilated before *Ca, and in a few cases primary-stressed *a; still productive (§4.4.1, Table 2: left to right but not on primary-stressed *a).
Primary-stressed *a usually does not dissimilate (Table 2); a few cases do ((61): *tamá-na > teme-n).
